Nature’s Vault

Why dig it up at all?

Most gold already changes hands on paper. Certificates, accounts and contracts trade while the metal itself sits untouched in a vault.

Nature’s Vault

Gold in the ground is real property.

As real property, it can be owned, divided and exchanged, without ever being touched.

Nature’s Vault

And the land above comes alive.

The gold rests in Nature’s Vault. Above it, the land is stewarded: soil restored, water protected, forests and communities given room to thrive, for generations.

Discover this new asset class
The RealGold DST

A new class of real property.

Fractional beneficial interests in perpetual mineral estates, structured as Delaware Statutory Trusts and designed to support Section 1031 treatment.

Real property

A deeded mineral estate, severed from the surface and held in fee simple.

Held in perpetuity

No forced exit timeline. The client decides when, or whether, to sell.

Owned, not operated

Value rests on the estate and the minerals in place, not on a business operating above it.

Real estate and gold. Two of humanity’s oldest ways of holding value, now held together.

Section 1031 treatment depends on individual circumstances, and the federal tax opinion is pending. Consult your own tax and legal advisors.

What Protects This Asset

Four layers. Each one a matter of record.

  1. Recorded titleFee-simple patented claim, surveyed and recorded in county records.
  2. Independent verificationResource established by a third-party technical report. The unit count is fixed by that report.
  3. Separate custodyThe mineral estate is held by the trust, under the DST trust agreement.
  4. Recorded covenantPerpetual non-extraction, binding every successor in title.

Every layer is documented in the due diligence binder.

Land Stewardship

Gold extraction destroys the earth. Gold preservation protects it.

The trust holds the mineral estate. Companion biological and social estates care for the land and the communities above it, for generations.
